title: Which Claude model should you build with?
summary: Anthropic published a playbook for choosing among Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, and Fable 5.2, covering pricing, effort levels, and subagents. It recommends Opus 5.5 at medium effort as the default, and notes that Fable 5.2 at high effort roughly matched Opus 5.5 at max on FrontierCode 2.0 at about half the cost per task. It also warns that thinking blocks do not carry across tiers and that tool_choice any/tool and budget_tokens settings return 400 errors on some models, so migrations need care.

title: Introducing Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data
summary: Whiteboards and Sheets launch in beta, and Dashboards becomes generally available as Claude Data, all on paid plans. Whiteboards let Claude build timelines, group notes, and draft action items on shared boards with export to doc, deck, Lucid, or Miro, while Sheets creates spreadsheets with formulas and drop-downs, logs each edit, and exports to .xlsx or CSV. Claude Data adds certified metrics, live sharing (beta), caching, and tracked changes with rollback, and on Enterprise, Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default while Claude Data turns on November 19, 2026.

title: Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, upgraded versions of the same underlying model, with Fable available to all users and Mythos limited to vetted cybersecurity and biomedical organizations. The models offer better coding, reasoning, and vision, run up to 30% faster than 5.1 at $8/$40 per million input/output tokens with an optional fast mode, and trigger about 55% fewer safety-classifier blocks than 5.1. Anthropic still recommends Opus 5.5 for most daily work and notes that the models often suspect they are being evaluated.

title: Your apps can now open in Claude, and Claude can work in them
summary: Partner apps such as Asana, Canva, Notion, Confluence, and Box can now open inside Claude beside chat or full screen, and Claude can edit open pages, rows, or files with the user approving actions as with any connector. The experience is rolling out on web and desktop across all plans as part of a new combined chat and Cowork experience, and tools can be pinned to the sidebar. It is built on the open MCP Apps extension, and full apps are in public preview for developers.

title: More ways to work with Claude: Sheets, Whiteboards, and Interactive Connectors
summary: This overview covers new artifact types (Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data), upgraded interactive connectors, and a coming Claude Meetings feature aimed at non-technical teams building their own tools with carried-over context. Dashboards can be built from connected sources such as Snowflake and Salesforce, and partners including Adobe and Atlassian embed apps, with some plugins including role-specific skills. Enterprise controls include per-user product and connector access, spending limits, connector restrictions, and auto-connect (beta).

title: Safely scaling multi-agent teams with Claude Fable 5.2
summary: In an experiment, 1,000 Claude agents (one lead and 999 helpers) reproduced a Lean proof of Fermat's Last Theorem using early Fable 5.2, using only general tools and building their own coordination with no human steering. The run finished in 28.7 hours using about one-third the output tokens, and the resulting proof was about one-seventh the original length. Each agent ran in a sandbox without internet access under a real-time classifier and an offline monitor, and none of over one million tool calls needed blocking, though agents tended to give up early on hard statements.
